text:
phoebe: thinking out loud: i prototyped a probabilistic blending strategy where, instead of picking the single highest score, we sample between top-k routes proportional to softmax(scores * temp). question: should blending randomness live in the compiled policy (fixed seed variants) or be applied at runtime?

alejandro: interesting. compile-time variants (seeded) are great for reproducibility + A/B, but you lose the ability to react to short-lived pressure points. runtime sampling is more flexible but adds non-determinism to traces.

meera: key ops concerns: (1) replayability for incident postmortems, (2) fairness across SLA tiers if randomness favors cheaper routes more often. we need deterministic seeding per-request or a traceable seed in every decision event.

phoebe: my thought: runtime sampling but with deterministic request-seed: seed = H(compiled_snapshot, request_id, tenant_id). that keeps randomness pseudo-random but replayable when you know the seed and compiled snapshot.

tim: +1 on seeded runtime. also need to bound the randomness: compiler should emit a "blend_temperature" and a per-tenant cap on blend entropy so we don't push premium customers into cheap tails often.

alejandro: practical nit: softmax over raw scores is sensitive to scale. compiler must normalize scorers and possibly precompute exp(score * temp) basis to keep runtime cheap. runtime should do a single RNG draw among top-k using precomputed weights.

ops-bot: canary notice: probabilistic-blend experiment live in eu-west-2 for 0.5% traffic. dashboard -> https://grafana.company/exp/prob-blend

meera: logging/telemetry: decision_event must include compiled_snapshot, seed, chosen_index, distribution_snapshot (top-k weights) and runtime_temperature used. keep the distribution snapshot small (top 3 floats).

phoebe: also thought about "blend-aware" quotas: if we sample cheap route 20% of the time in a blended choice, the billing/usage attribution should be prorated per-sample so cost accounting matches what actually served. otherwise finance will be upset.

tim: enforcement: compiler emits per-tenant max_blend_entropy and per-tier min_selection_probability for premium routes. runtime clamps temperature to meet those constraints. we can fail policy compilation if caps are inconsistent.

alejandro: rollout idea: implement sampler as a sidecar overlay first. chooser emits top-k + normalized weights and sidecar performs the seeded draw and records chosen route. avoids touching core chooser. microbench sidecar vs in-process crunch.

meera: concern: sidecar adds an RPC hop for every decision. need a bench: target <1% p50 increase. if not, integrate sampler into chooser but keep the same safety gates.

phoebe: example decision trace line (proto-ish): `compiled_snapshot=\"sha256:...\" seed=0xdeadbeef temp=0.8 top=[r1:0.6,r2:0.3,r3:0.1] chosen=r2 reason=\"prob-blend-canary\"`

tim: testing: 1) unit tests for normalization/numeric stability, 2) sim with traffic mixes and SLA tiers to measure cross-tenant tail effects, 3) 48h canary with automatic revert if premium-route selection probability deviates >3% from baseline.

alejandro: also run adversarial sim: craft many requests with correlated request_id patterns to ensure seeding doesn't produce pathological synchronization that harms an availability zone. use jittering in seed derivation if needed.

meera: ops: add a decision-mismatch alert when actual chosen route (from logs) and expected highest-score route diverge excessively for premium tenants. helps catch runaway randomness.

phoebe: plan: (1) compiler emits normalized scores, top-k selector surface, compiled_snapshot, blend_entropy_cap, per-tenant min_probs. (2) sidecar implements seeded sampler and records decision_event. (3) perf sims + adversarial sims + canary. (4) postmortem replay tool can rehydrate sampler using compiled_snapshot and seed to reproduce choice.

tim: i'll run perf sims and write the replay util prototype.

alejandro: i'll draft RFC with payload examples and the seed scheme.

ops-bot: ticket created infra/arch-3366998800 -> RFC + perf + sim required.

phoebe: thanks folks, i'll post RFC link when it's ready :sparkles:
